items.text: Do not accuse your parents, except for plotting treason, rebellion, or revolt.
items.citation: Gyeongguk Daejeon, 刑典 告尊長 1
items.quote: 子孫·妻妾·奴婢告父母·家長, 除謀叛·逆·反外, 絞。 — Descendants, wives, concubines, and servants who accuse parents or household heads, except for plotting treason, rebellion, or revolt, are strangled.
items.conflict: Absolute ban on accusation suppresses truth and violates biblical rebuke (Lev 19:17; Matt 18:15).

work: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Books of Revenue and Punishments: household registers, proper
heading: 經國大典 戶典 · 田宅 전택 · Fields and Houses (incl. inheritance disputes) … 戶典 田宅 6

items.text: Pass the merit field to your descendants, not to outsiders or collateral kin.
items.quote: 功臣田, 傳子孫 — Merit fields pass to sons and grandsons.

items.text: Give the heir who bears the burden of ancestral rites an extra one-third of the merit field.
items.quote: 承重者, 加三分之一 — The heir who bears the burden receives an additional third.

items.text: If you, a daughter, hold merit land, after your death it must pass to the descendants who carry on the family name, not to your own children of another surname.
items.quote: 女子身死後, 移給繼姓子孫 — After the daughter dies, transfer to descendants who continue the family name.

items.text: If your legal wife has no descendants, pass the merit field to your son by a commoner concubine.
items.quote: 嫡室無子孫者, 傳良妾子孫 — If the legal wife has no children, pass to the sons of a commoner concubine.

items.text: If you have only a son by a low-born concubine who is the heir, give him thirty kyŏl of ritual land for the ancestral rites and surrender the rest to the state.
items.quote: 賤妾子孫承重者, 只給祭田三十結, 其餘屬公 — The low-born concubine's heir receives only thirty kyŏl of ritual land; the rest goes to the state.

items.text: If a descendant who received the merit field commits a crime and his property is to be confiscated, transfer the field to another descendant so it remains in the family.
items.quote: 傳受子孫若被罪應收者, 移給他子孫 — If the recipient grandson is convicted and his property confiscated, transfer to other descendants.

items.text: Pass the house containing the ancestral shrine to the descendant who performs the ancestral rites.
items.quote: 立廟家舍, 傳於主祭子孫 — The house with the ancestral temple passes to the descendant who performs the rites.

items.text: If you jointly hold your parents' fields or houses with a sibling, do not refuse his claim by pleading the five-year limit; let the dispute be heard and divided justly.
items.quote: 父母田宅合執者, 不限年 — Those who jointly hold parents' fields and houses are not limited by the five-year rule.

work: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Books of Revenue and Punishments: household registers, proper
heading: 經國大典 刑典 · 賤妻妾子女 천처첩자녀 · Children of Base-born Wives and Concubines … 刑典 賤妻妾子女 2

items.text: Report your child to the Slave Office, verify and record the case, transfer documents to the Ministry of War, and enroll them in the supplementary units before they turn sixteen.
items.quote: 其父告掌隷院, 覈實錄案, 移文兵曹, 屬補充隊 — The father reports to the Slave Office, verifies and records the case, transfers document to the Ministry of War, and enrolls in the supplementary units.

items.text: If the father is dead, report your stepchild to the Slave Office, verify and record the case, transfer documents to the Ministry of War, and enroll them in the supplementary units.
items.quote: 無父, 則嫡母 — If no father, then the legitimate mother.

items.text: If there is no father and no legitimate mother, report your sibling to the Slave Office, verify and record the case, transfer documents to the Ministry of War, and enroll them in the supplementary units.
items.quote: 無嫡母, 則同生 — If no legitimate mother, then the siblings.

items.text: If there is no father, no legitimate mother, and no sibling, report your grandchild to the Slave Office, verify and record the case, transfer documents to the Ministry of War, and enroll them in the supplementary units.
items.quote: 無同生, 則祖父母告 — If no siblings, then the grandparents report.

items.text: If the child is not born of your own slave or your wife's slave, provide a healthy person of suitable age to redeem the child, and if the owner refuses, report to the officials.
items.quote: 皆贖身（以無病年歲相當者贖。 本主若不聽, 則告官。） — All are redeemed; redeem with a healthy person of suitable age; if the owner refuses, report to officials.

items.text: Do not inform against the child to have them returned to low status.
items.quote: 有服親, 毋得陳告 — Relatives with mourning obligations may not report them.

work: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Books of Revenue and Punishments: household registers, proper
heading: 經國大典 刑典 · 私賤 사천 · Private Slaves (incl. division of slaves among heirs) … 刑典 私賤 10

items.text: Give the share of slaves the deceased child would have received to his descendants; if he left no descendants, his share lapses.
items.quote: 未分奴婢, 勿論子女存歿分給。身歿無子孫者, 不在此限。

items.text: When slaves are too few for the prescribed shares, give equal shares to legitimate children before any extra is given.
items.quote: 未滿分數者, 均給嫡子女。

items.text: After equal shares, give any remainder first to the lineage heir, then to others in order of age.
items.quote: 若有餘數, 先給承重子, 又有餘, 則以長幼次序給之。

items.text: When dividing parents' slaves, give the lineage heir one fifth more than each legitimate child.
items.quote: 父母奴婢 — 承重子: 加五分之一。

items.text: Give a child of a free concubine one seventh of a legitimate child's share, but only from the father's slaves, not the mother's.
items.quote: 良妾子女: 七分之一。嫡母奴婢, 則否。

items.text: Give a child of a lowborn concubine one tenth of the parents' slaves.
items.quote: 父母奴婢 — 賤妾子女: 十分之一。

items.text: If the deceased had no legitimate children, divide the slaves equally among the children of a free concubine, and give the lineage heir an extra one fifth.
items.quote: 嫡無子女者奴婢 — 良妾子女: 平分。 承重子, 則加五分之一。

items.text: After paying the prescribed shares, return the remainder of a childless legitimate mother's slaves to her natal family.
items.quote: 無子女嫡母奴婢 — 餘還本族。

items.text: Give the lineage heir one seventh of a legitimate mother's slaves, but do not give more than three slaves.
items.quote: 無子有女嫡母奴婢 — 承重子, 七分之一, 毋過三口。

items.text: Give an adopted child one seventh of the adoptive parents' slaves if there are no legitimate children, one tenth if there are, and all if adopted before age three.
items.quote: 無子女養父母奴婢 — 養子女: 七分之一。（三歲前, 則全給。 ... 嫡有子女養父母奴婢 — 養子女: 十分之一。 三歲前, 則七分之一。

items.text: Do not divide the slaves of one who died without heirs among adoptees and serving descendants until three years have passed.
items.quote: 無後身死人奴婢, 收養·使孫等三年內, 毋得相分。

items.text: When dividing slaves, use an official document, except when the division is made by mutual agreement among parents, grandparents, maternal grandparents, wife's parents, husband, wife, concubine, and siblings.
items.quote: 父母·祖父母·外祖父母·妻父母·夫·妻·妾及同生和會分執外, 用官署文記。

work: Gyeongguk Daejeon, Books of Revenue and Punishments: household registers, proper
heading: 經國大典 刑典 · 禁制 금제 · Prohibitions … 刑典 禁制 15

items.text: Remain chaste and faithful to your husband; do not commit misconduct.
items.quote: 士族婦女失行者...錄案 — If a noble woman commits misconduct, it is recorded.

items.text: Do not take a third husband; preserve your chastity for your deceased husbands.
items.quote: 更適三夫者同 — Remarrying three husbands is treated the same as misconduct.
items.conflict: Bible permits remarriage after death of spouse (Rom 7:2-3; 1 Cor 7:39).

items.text: Once you have accepted a marriage contract for your child, do not consent to marry them to another.
items.quote: 己受婚書而再許他人成婚者, 其主婚者, 論罪, 離異。 — If one who has accepted a marriage contract consents to another, the arranger is punished and divorced.

items.text: Do not give your household's slaves or fields to temples or shamans.
items.quote: 私奴婢·田地施納寺社·巫覡者...屬公 — Those who give private slaves or fields to temples or shamans are punished, and the slaves and fields are confiscated to the state.

items.text: Do not go to Buddhist temples.
items.quote: 婦女上寺者 — Women who go to Buddhist temples are punished.

items.text: Do not personally perform sacrifices at mountains, rivers, or tutelary shrines.
items.quote: 親行野祭·山川·城隍·祠廟祭者 — personally performing field sacrifices or sacrifices at mountains, rivers, or tutelary shrines.
